subject: multiple random effect blocks and the decov prior?

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: multiple random effect blocks and the decov prior?
parts:
Hi!

Suppose I have a model with two blocks of random effects:

y ~ 1 + cov1 + cov2 + cov3 + (cov1 + cov2 | grouping1 ) + ( cov3 | grouping2 )

So I intend to fit 3 random effects out of which the first two are modeled as correlated while the third is independent of the others.

How do I set the prior_covariance then? Can I give it a list of length of decov priors?

Thanks.

Best,
Sebastian

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: multiple random effect blocks and the decov prior?
parts:
On Wednesday, November 2, 2016 at 4:56:13 AM UTC-4, Sebastian Weber wrote:

Suppose I have a model with two blocks of random effects:

y ~ 1 + cov1 + cov2 + cov3 + (cov1 + cov2 | grouping1 ) + ( cov3 | grouping2 )

So I intend to fit 3 random effects out of which the first two are modeled as correlated while the third is independent of the others.

How do I set the prior_covariance then? Can I give it a list of length of decov priors?

You can't supply a list of decov priors but you can specify a decov prior with vectors as its arguments. For (cov1 + cov2 | grouping), there will be 1 scale parameter, 1 concentration parameter, and 1 regularization (LKJ) parameter. For (cov3 | grouping), there will be 1 scale parameter only. Thus, I think you can pass to decov a vector of length two for its shape and / or scale arguments for the gamma priors on the scale parameters. Then, you would need a scalar for each of the regularization and concentration arguments.

Ben

So you mean I could do

decov(2, 1, c(1, 1), c(1/2, 1/4))

In order to get a LKJ which pulls towards identity (the 2), haven the dirichlet spread out evenly the fractions and essentially put an exponential on the three random effects?

... but this confuses me as to what now exactly the total variance is wrt to which the simplex vector spreads the total variance. In case the total variance is to be understood by block, which I think makes sense, then the LKJ and the "spreading" parameter should be vectors of length 2 as well, but as I understand you this is not the case?

Yes, the total variance is block by block. But if you have a 1x1 block in the case of ( cov3 | grouping2 ), then there is no correlation matrix and no simplex; just a scale with a gamma prior.

Ben

On Thursday, November 3, 2016 at 3:31:39 AM UTC-4, Sebastian Weber wrote:
Ah... OK. Just for my understanding: If I were to use a model slightly more complex as


y ~ 1 + cov1 + cov2 + cov3 + (cov1 + cov2 | grouping1 ) + ( cov1 + cov3 | grouping2 )

then I would give to decov a vector of length two in each argument. This would parametrize the per-block total variance, LKJ regularization and spread.

Just a last one: Is the intercept implicitly added to the random effect parts? So (cov1 + cov2 | grouping1 )  is indeed (1 + cov1 + cov2 | grouping1 )? If I would like to get rid of the intercept I would have to write (0 + cov1 + cov2 | grouping1 ), right?

Yes, although that is inherited from lme4. A slight difference is that Stan should throw an error message if you have multiple intercept deviations from the same grouping factor. So, (cov1 | grouping1) + (cov2 | grouping1) is an error but (cov1 | grouping1) + (0 + cov2 | grouping1) is not.

Ben
